sampling_plan.purpose: Treat Norling as reinforcement after D’Amelio and extract progressively less unless a real delta survives comparison.

observations.summary: Norling covers the same broad foundation as D’Amelio, then adds practical exercises, reflections, unusual/sloped views, and a mechanical projection appendix.
Horizon, eye level, convergence, one/two-point setups, object blocking, spacing, and basic shadows substantially reinforce the D’Amelio candidate foundation.
Extending parallel edge families in an already-made image to recover vanishing points and camera eye level is a distinct reverse-analysis capability not present in the D’Amelio cards.
Norling makes the two horizontal vanishing points a coupled consequence of one viewer/object rotation; this strengthens the existing orientation Pattern without requiring a separate card.
Level-surface reflections are constructively located by equal mirrored distance and preserve the object’s perspective direction families; the baseline has no reflection card.
The hill-road “false eye-level” is a practical reframe of the already-held inclined-plane geometry rather than a new independent foundation.
Norling’s plan/elevation mechanical method projects exact orthographic geometry from a station point into perspective and is absent from the cumulative baseline.
The source is best treated as full Review plus targeted PASS: most material should confirm/patch D’Amelio while only a few capabilities become new cards.

rationale: The structural sample confirms heavy overlap with D’Amelio but also reveals three credible missing capabilities—reverse analysis of an existing image, level-plane reflections, and exact plan/elevation projection. Complete Gate 2 is justified to separate those deltas from reinforcement and to catch contradictions before authoring.
